text:
maya: Hey folks — short question. We have a CI pipeline that needs to create projects and attach billing for new customer sandboxes. Currently the pipeline runs with a service account that has Organization Project Creator at org-level. Is there a cleaner least-privilege approach?

aj: Prefer not to give org-level Project Creator if we can avoid it. Can the pipeline instead use a folder-scoped role and IAM Conditions to limit what it can create?

maya: We want automated project creation under folder /customers/sandboxes only. Thought was: grant roles/resourcemanager.projectCreator at folder scope + condition to require parent == folders/12345. But not sure if folder-scoped projectCreator works in GCP?

devon: Folder-scoped project creation works: you can grant resourcemanager.projects.create on the folder. But most teams do org-level projectCreator because of quota/billing friction. If you lock folder and use a condition on billingAccount == 'BILLING_ID' you can restrict which billing account they can attach.

leo: Quick note: IAM Conditions don't support all attributes at folder creation time. You can condition on resource.name and request.auth, and there are attributes like resource.parent. For the billing account restriction you'd probably enforce via organization policy or a short-lived approval step that chooses the billing account.

maya: Hmm, so options look like: (1) keep org Project Creator for pipeline SA but rotate creds frequently / make ephemeral, (2) use folder-scoped create + org policy that forces billing account whitelist, or (3) have pipeline call an internal service that holds org-level perms and enforces checks. Which is least operational pain?

aj: (2) is nice because it limits blast radius. OrgPolicy orgpolicy/constraints/gcp.resourceLocations and constraints/compute.vmExternalIp can help too. For billing, org policy can restrict which billing accounts can be attached.

security_lead: +1 for (2). Also add an approval webhook in the pipeline for new projects > A simple step that logs request id and developer email to audit logs and requires an SRE or Finance approval for non-default billing. That keeps auditable trail without giving broad org perms.

devon: If you want to avoid human approvals, you can implement a short-lived token pattern: pipeline calls a privileged service with svc acct X that has org-level projectCreator, but that service only issues a signed one-time token after policy checks. Works well if you already have internal vault/invoke infra.

maya: Thanks — one more: what's the minimal IAM binding we can give to the pipeline SA so it can programmatically set IAM on the created project so it attaches the correct editors/owners?

leo: After project creation, the pipeline will need roles/resourcemanager.projectIamAdmin on that project to bind roles. But you can avoid that by using the privileged service approach to create and set IAM atomically. Otherwise the pipeline needs iam.serviceAccounts.actAs for any SA it uses.

org-audit-bot: [automated] Created audit entry: action=project_create_request, actor=maya, request_id=req-2026504321, folder=folders/12345

aj: TL;DR suggestion: give pipeline SA folder-level project create + org policy whitelist for billing accounts. Add a pipeline check that refuses to use non-whitelisted billing. If you can't control billing via org policy, put the billing attachment step behind the privileged service.

maya: Perfect — we'll prototype folder-scoped create + org policy. I'll open a PR for the infra change and tag security for review. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:

security_lead: Please include the audit log sink config in the PR (so Finance sees all attachments). Approve in principle; will do a formal review once PR is up.

maya: Will do. Filing infra PR and tagging @security_lead and @aj.
